Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like the end of 2017, probably December 2017 or January 2018, based on the following.

- The fed funds rate is 0.66%, which is too low for late 2017 (about 1.3%) and fits late 2016 or early 2017 better. Fed funds was about 0.66% in December 2016, when the target range was 0.50–0.75 after the December hike.
- The 10-year yield is 2.49%, which fits December 2016 (about 2.45%).
- The 2-year yield is 1.22%, which fits December 2016 (about 1.2%).
- Unemployment of 4.7% fits November or December 2016.
- Headline CPI of 2.1% fits December 2016, and core CPI of 2.2% also fits.
- US large-cap equity returned 20% over 12 months, which is high for 2016 (about 12%). Counting back from November 2016, though, 12-month equity returns were about 8%, so that part does not fit well. Emerging-market equity returned 25.7% over 12 months, which also seems high for December 2016.
- The dollar is down 8% YoY, which suggests 2017 and not 2016, when the dollar was rising.
- Rechecking 2017: unemployment was 4.7% in March–April 2017, with fed funds at 0.66% in Feb 2017 (0.55%) and Mar 2017 (0.79%). Neither month matches exactly. However, the 20y+ drawdown is 15%, the 6-month gold return is −10.6%, and the 3-month 10-year yield change is +0.65, all of which fit the post-election selloff.
- Equity 12-month return of 20% fits the period to March 2017 (S&P about +17%). The VIX at 11.88 also fits Feb–Mar 2017 (about 12).
- Rechecking the dollar: it was down 8% YoY by mid-2017, but the YoY comparison from early 2017 is closer to flat.

This leaves the date uncertain between February and April 2017. Gold rose 4.8% in the month, which fits February 2017 (+3–4%). Emerging-market equity rose 5.9% in the month, which fits February 2017 (+3.5%) or March 2017 (+2.5%). Developed ex-US equity rose 3.7% in the month, which fits February 2017 (+2.5%). The 10-year yield at 2.49% fits end-February 2017 (2.39%) and end-March 2017 (2.40%) less well, but December 2016 fits at 2.45%. Unemployment was 4.7% in February 2017 per the later figure of 4.7. The 3-month change in CPI of +0.62 also fits the period to January or February 2017.

I'll go with February 2017.
